thread:
deploy-bot: ALERT: auth-service high 5xx rate in prod (us-east-1). 5xx spike starting 12:07 UTC. see /alerts/1852345678

mike-sre: seeing a wave of 502/503 from auth-introspect. users hitting generate endpoints get 401s. - I’m on it.

anna-support: customer CH-342 (chris-customer) just escalated: `All requests suddenly failing with 401` since 12:10. They say it started after a background key rotation earlier today.

chris-customer: @anna-support yep, we got a heads-up about a rotation but our refresh didn't change. Example curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token-from-12:00>\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -i` returns `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` with body `{"error":"invalid_token"}`. We still have some traffic up to 12:05 then boom.

mike-sre: grabbing logs. Looks like `key-rotation-job` ran at 11:58 and we have introspect errors starting ~12:07 when introspect started returning 502 from oauth-proxy.

jess-platform: timeline: rotation job kicked off on canary at 11:30, then rollout to prod at 11:58 via k8s job `rotation-run-2026-03-15`. No manual approvals. autoscaler and canary checks reported green.

sam-engineering: digging into rotation job logs. Found this snippet from the rotation controller:
```
INFO 11:58:20 Rotating key for client_id=redwood-sdk
INFO 11:58:22 Deleting old key id=ak_OLD_9f3
INFO 11:58:23 Creating new key id=ak_NEW_7b2
INFO 11:58:24 Marked new key active
```
But the job also called `introspect-cache:clear` which apparently triggered a cascade to oauth-proxy.

olga-security: important note: rotation job is supposed to write both new key and add it to the `key-accept` list for a 5m grace period. logs show `Adding to accept-list failed: 409 conflict` around 11:58:22. Might be a race where deletion and accept-list update overlapped.

mike-sre: oauth-proxy health shows: `upstream introspect` started returning 502 due to connection resets to introspect service. If introspect fails, token validation falls back to cache which had been cleared by the job. So tokens invalid until introspect recovers or keys accepted. That explains 401s.

anna-support: customer update to CH-342: sent temporary mitigation steps: "Please retry after 15 minutes. We're investigating. If you have the new key we can accept it early; otherwise we will re-issue and notify." They replied they're seeing errors for internal users and a small percentage of external customers.

sam-engineering: repro steps for us:
1. Issue token using pre-rotation key.
2. Immediately curl introspect endpoint `/oauth/introspect` with that token -> before rotation returns 200. After rotation + cache-clear -> 502/401.

Example repro curl: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://auth.redwood.example/oauth/introspect \
  -u \"client:secret\" \
  -d \"token=eyJhbGci...\"
```
Response (post rotation):
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"error":"upstream_error","message":"connection reset by peer"}
```

mike-sre: immediate mitigation: pausing key-rotation job (kubectl pause job rotation-run-2026-03-15), re-seeding introspect cache with previously known good key material, and restarting oauth-proxy pods. Doing now.

deploy-bot: ACTION | paused job rotation-run-2026-03-15 (initiated by mike-sre)

mike-sre: restarted oauth-proxy pods. Observability: 5xx rate dropped from 12% to 0.8% in ~90s. Introspect returning 200 again for old tokens.

anna-support: notified CH-342 and 4 other customers who reported issues. Instructed to retry; most report success now. CH-342 says internal dashboards are back.

olga-security: postmortem initial notes: root cause appears to be a race in rotation controller where it deleted old key before accept-list insertion completed; simultaneously the job cleared the introspect cache which removed fallback; this produced a window where oauth-proxy couldn't validate tokens and upstream introspect was flapping. Also missing canary that tests introspect path under load.

sam-engineering: stack snippet from rotation controller where bug likely lives:
```go
// pseudocode
if err := deleteOldKey(oldID); err != nil { return err }
if err := addToAcceptList(newID); err != nil { return err }
// bug: should add to accept list before deleting old key
```

jess-platform: immediate mitigation checklist I'm creating:
- Add pre-check in rotation job to ensure `accept-list` write succeeds before removing old key.
- Disable cache-clear during rotation or make it a safe operation (drain-first).
- Add canary test that runs a quick introspect + generate path against canary tokens before rollouts.
- Add alert for `rotation-job` errors on `accept-list` writes.

olga-security: also need to notify security/compliance: any key deletions without grace violate policy. We need an incident report for customers and auditors.

chris-customer: appreciate the quick response. Could you add an opt-in flag for customers to choose zero-downtime rotation mode? We're willing to do a small integration to avoid surprises.

jess-platform: yes, we'll explore `zero-downtime` mode. longer-term we should have dual-write acceptance window and a staged cache invalidation.

mike-sre: follow-up actions (short):
- revert rotation-run-2026-03-15 in job history and block automated rollouts until fix deployed (in progress)
- add alert for `introspect` 5xx spike linked to rotation ops (in progress)
- coordinate with support on customer comms (anna)

anna-support: customer comms draft: "We experienced a temporary authentication outage due to an automated key rotation that removed a previously valid key before the new key was fully accepted by our token verification path. We paused the rotation, restarted proxy pods, and service has recovered. We're working on code and process fixes. We will follow up with a postmortem and timeline." Any edits?

olga-security: add note about mitigations taken and whether any keys were exposed (none). Also indicate whether any tokens were accepted incorrectly (no evidence of misuse).

sam-engineering: plan for fix: reorder operations, add transactional semantics or two-phase commit for rotation, and maintain cached keys until accept-list write confirmed + health-check introspect path before clearing cache. ETA for code change: 1 day, test + canary: 2 days, rollout: 3 days.

mike-sre: closing notes: system recovered at 12:17 UTC after rolling back rotation and restarting oauth-proxy. Total customer impact window ~7–12 minutes for affected tokens. Logging saved for postmortem.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT | resolved (mitigated) 12:17 UTC — see incident ticket INC-20260315-24 for follow-up tasks.

chris-customer: thanks everyone. Please keep me posted on the postmortem.

anna-support: will follow up with CH-342 and other affected customers with timeline + postmortem when ready.

jess-platform: scheduling immediate postmortem meeting 13:00 UTC today. Required: rotation-controller owners, SRE, security, support.

olga-security: reminder to capture runbook updates and add integration test that simulates key rotation under load.

mike-sre: adding runbook blurb now: "If automated rotation causes 5xx/401 spike: pause job, restart oauth-proxy, re-seed cache, notify support, roll back rotation".

anna-support: thanks team — closing thread for active triage. Will re-open if we see regression.
